summary: Robert S. Nelson is a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Rice University (circa 1965–1969) and New York University (circa 1970–1978). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (circa 1974–2005) and held a post at Yale University (circa 2005).

Robert Warren Clark works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under supervisor Karen C. Lang and adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao, alongside training under traditional teachers including Geshe Dawa Sangpo, Thubten Yeshe, and Henepola Gunaratana.
Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist who studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1910 to 1913. He held an academic post at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, from circa 1914 to 1930.

Robin Coningham is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at King's College (1985–1994) and earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge (circa 1989–1994). He held posts at the University of Bradford (circa 1994–2005) and Durham University (2005).

Roderick Chisholm was a philosopher who studied at Harvard University from circa 1938 to 1942. He held academic posts at Brown University from circa 1947 to 1986 and at the University of Massachusetts Amherst from circa 1986 to 1996.

Roderick Whitfield is a scholar in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the British Museum from circa 1968 to 1984 and at SOAS University of London as professor and emeritus from circa 1984 to 2002.

Roger R. Jackson studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, he was Associate Professor of Religion at Carleton College from circa 1989 to 2016.

Roger T. Ames, a specialist in philosophy and Sinology, studied at the University of British Columbia and National Taiwan University. He held posts at the University of Hawaii (circa 1978–2016), SUNY, and Peking University (circa 2016), and edited Philosophy East and West.
Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn between circa 1990 and 1997. In circa 1999, he held an assistant professor post at the University of Marburg.

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who studied at the University of Salzburg from circa 1996 to 2002. He held academic posts at Heidelberg University from circa 2014 to 2017 and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich around 2017.

Rolf Alfred Stein, a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology, studied in Berlin, INALCO, and under Marcel Granet and Paul Pelliot, among others. He held posts at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France (1965–1981).

Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna (circa 2004–2010) under Helmut Tauscher. He also studied under traditional teachers Tsultrim Gyatso and Khenpo Chodrak Tenphel.

Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and completed her doctorate under A. L. Basham at SOAS. She held posts at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, and Cornell University.
Ron Garry is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His education includes studying under the traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied under teacher Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and also studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. His academic appointments include serving as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and as an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser works in religious studies, philosophy, and other fields, and studied under traditional teacher Koshin Ogui in 1985. He held posts at Loyola University Chicago until circa 1997 and at San Francisco State University from circa 1997.

Ronald Egan is a Sinologist who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University (circa 1970–1977). He held posts at Harvard, Wellesley College, the University of California, Santa Barbara as Professor of Chinese Literature (circa 1987–2012), and Stanford University (circa 2012).

Ronald James Dziwenka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his studies by 2010 under doctoral supervisor Jiang Wu and committee members Noel Pinnington, Chia-lin Pao Tao, and Yetta M. Goodman.

Ronald M. Davidson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1976–1985) under teachers including Lewis Lancaster and Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held a post at Fairfield University around 1990.
